rename.from: Queries order is not repeatable causing concurrency issues
rename.to: Queries execution order is not guaranteed causing concurrency issues

body:
The problem comes from https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/master/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/unitofwork.py#L441

`UOWTransaction` has an attribute named `dependencies` of type set. In my example it could be equal to `{(SaveUpdateAll(mapped class MyTable->my_table), DeleteAll(mapped class MyTable->my_table)), (SaveUpdateAll(mapped class MyTable2->my_table2), DeleteAll(mapped class MyTable2->my_table2))}`.

A `set` is supposed to be ordered, but here it contains tuples of objects, so the order is determined by the objects' locations in memory, which vary over time.

To make the updates order deterministic, you can replace:

```python
for rec in topological.sort(self.dependencies, postsort_actions):
    rec.execute(self)
```

with:

```python
for rec in sorted(
    topological.sort(self.dependencies, postsort_actions),
    key=lambda a: a.mapper.tables[0].name
):
    rec.execute(self)
```

Of course, the `key` I am suggesting here is not the one that should be used. It is just a quick hack to demonstrate how the problem could be fixed, but I am not aware enough of SQLAlchemy internals to provide a `key` that makes sense.

Hi, thanks for the great mcve and for pointing to the probably cause!

It's probably irrelevant in this case, but are you using the 1.3 series or the 1.4 beta version of sqlalchemy?

so, this issue has a little bit of similarity to #2501 but not that much.  in #2501 the issue is that the determined sort still does not accommodate for an edge case where rows with unique constraints are being swapped, and users have to use flush() to sort it out for now.

in SQLAlchemy unit of work, the determined sorting is as follows:

1. sorting is first performed at the level of target table, using a topological algorithm that uses mapper configurational structures to determine dependencies, these are the relationship() construct as well as some inheritance-related structures

2. if there are no dependency cycles between the target tables, the flush proceeds as:

   a. within a particular table, INSERT operations are processed in the order in which objects were add()'ed
   b. within a particular table, UPDATE and DELETE operations are processed in primary key order

SQLAlchemy's "deterministic" system goes that far right now when there are no inter-row dependencies between tables or a table to itself.

3. if there are dependency cycles between target tables, the per-table lists of objects among the affected tables are broken out into per-object records which are then toplogically sorted against each other.   INSERTS, UPDATES and DELETES proceed in the ordering given in 2, but only within subsets of objects that were not otherwise dependent on each other.

the system is oriented towards *not* going into number 3 if at all possible, because this is a much less efficient road to travel.  it has to sort among all objects individually and also causes there to be lots more smaller operations of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE that can't be batched.   the UOW really wants to batch things as much as it can so that there are fewer calls to DBAPI execute() and the DBAPI can invoke for many rows using faster native operations.

so if we were to take your original proposal that .add() order would be honored among all INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE across all tables at once, we'd need to throw out item 2 altogether and have a more complicated per-item sort in all cases that would also be a whole new ballgame with new kinds of cycle-oriented issues coming up, etc.

your second proposal is closer to how this should be done, however it's not correct to "sort" the items coming back from topological sort because we are then unordering the answer it gave us.   toplogical.sort() has a "determnistic_order" flag so that if you give the items in a fixed order you will get the same answer every time, so to add this feature looks like:

```diff
@@ -422,6 +422,10 @@ class UOWTransaction(object):
     def execute(self):
         postsort_actions = self._generate_actions()
 
+        postsort_actions = sorted(
+            postsort_actions,
+            key=lambda item: item.sort_key,
+        )
         # sort = topological.sort(self.dependencies, postsort_actions)
         # print "--------------"
         # print "\ndependencies:", self.dependencies
@@ -438,7 +442,9 @@ class UOWTransaction(object):
                     n = set_.pop()
                     n.execute_aggregate(self, set_)
         else:
-            for rec in topological.sort(self.dependencies, postsort_actions):
+            for rec in topological.sort(
+                self.dependencies, postsort_actions, deterministic_order=True
+            ):
                 rec.execute(self)
 
     def finalize_flush_changes(self):

```

pretty easy.   the problem of course is that this is less performant, as we need to create a "sort_key" for all the unit of work objects (I have that in the patch), we have to add a sorted() step, and then the deterministic_order flag uses a homegrown OrderedSet that is faster than the one Python provides but still pretty slow compared to set().

We can try to take advantage of Python 3.7 ordered dictionaries to implement a new insert-order set that is more lightweight and I might prefer to do that first before implementing this.  nevertheless I will push up the review for this so that it can be worked on at some point however this is not highest priortity at the moment.    The above unit of work rules have been the same for about 15 years and this is the first time this issue has ever been reported, so I hope for the meantime you can stick with that flush() step in there.
note that the above fix does cause your test case to run without errors.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Send deterministic ordering into unit of work topological** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2388

As usual, thanks a lot for the detailed explanations @zzzeek. Adding a second `flush()` ([here](https://github.com/openmaraude/APITaxi/commit/44b3a8afbf8f5a755ddaded8c0746ffba22ce197)) was enough to fix the problem for me.

I have been using SQLAlchemy for probably 10 years or so for simple or more complex projects, and it is the first time I encounter the issue. I discovered this bug because one of my clients does the same API query 3 times instead of 1. Who knows why. On the one hand, I tend to agree that it is a very low priority issue. On the other hand, I believe it is not uncommon to update several objects from the same transaction in a concurrent application.
